course_outcomes: After the successful completion of the course the students will be able to:
CO1 Determine the rank of a matrix to investigate the existence and uniqueness of solutions, identify and
analyse system behaviour under different conditions.
CO2 Apply fundamental principles of Eigen values, Eigen vectors, diagonalization and quadratic forms,
enabling the analysis and interpretation of basic engineering problems.
CO3 Apply fundamental concepts such as partial derivatives, chain rule, local linear approximations and
optimization techniques to analyse and solve problems involving functions of two variables.
CO4 Compute multiple integrals and apply them to find areas and volumes of geometrical shapes, mass and
centre of gravity of plane laminas.
CO5 Describe functions using various series expansions such as Taylor series, Binomial series and Fourier

topics: System of linear equations - Solution by Gauss elimination - Row Echelon form and Rank
of a matrix - Fundamental theorem for linear systems of homogeneous and
nonhomogeneous (without proof) - Homogeneous linear system - Non homogeneous
linear system.
Eigen values and Eigen vectors - Properties of Eigen values - Diagonalization of matrices -
Orthogonal transformation and orthogonal matrices - Quadratic forms and their Canonical
forms.
Concept of limit and continuity of functions of two variables - Partial derivatives of first and
higher order - Implicit partial differentiation - Local linear approximations - Chain rule for
derivatives and partial derivatives - Relative maxima and minima of function of two
variables (finding relative extrema only).

Double integrals (Cartesian) - Reversing the order of integration - Change of
coordinates (Cartesian to Polar) - Finding areas and volume using double integrals -
Mass and centre of gravity of inhomogeneous laminas using double integral - Triple
integrals - Volume calculated as triple integral - Triple integral in cylindrical and
spherical coordinates (computations involving spheres and cylinders only).
Taylor series and Maclaurin series - Binomial series - Fourier series - Euler
formulae - Convergence of Fourier series - Half Range sine and cosine series.

Guest lectures (online) from industry personnel / R&D organizations (National /
